problem_statement: The delivered Active task view initially sorts by creation date, so saved priority and its mouse drag affordance are hidden until users discover the Priority/highest-first sort combination; the decorative grip also does not act as the exclusive drag origin, and completed GitHub work remains recorded as open.
desired_outcome: Make saved priority the intuitive initial Active ordering, expose a clearly visible dedicated mouse drag grip immediately, preserve all authoritative reorder and Completed-sort behavior, and reconcile completed GitHub issue state with exact evidence.

personas.name: Personal task-list user
needs: Create a private account and return through a secure session.
Capture, revise, prioritize, complete, and reactivate personal tasks.
See active and completed work separately on desktop and mobile-sized viewports.
Trust that task data persists locally and remains inaccessible to other users.

personas.name: Local application operator
needs: Start the complete application with Docker Compose and required local configuration.
Begin with an empty database and retain PostgreSQL data through ordinary container replacement.
Diagnose operation through clean, human-readable rolling logs.

primary_journeys.outcome: The user creates an account and starts an authenticated task-management session.
steps: Open Sign Up and submit a display name, email, and password.
Receive a success indication and return to Login without being automatically signed in.
Submit the normalized email and password.
Arrive on the Active tab with the signed-in display name visible.

primary_journeys.outcome: The user immediately sees and maintains a correctly validated, prioritized, and optionally re-sorted active task list.
steps: Open Active and see Priority highest-first selected with saved priority order and a visible grip on every task.
Create a task with a required title and description and see it immediately at highest priority.
Edit an active task without changing its creation time or priority.
Press and hold a task grip with the mouse, drag to a new position, release, and retain the authoritative order after reload.
Choose another allowed Active sort key and direction when desired; reorder grips are absent outside Priority highest-first.
Cancel or confirm deletion through a confirmation dialog.

primary_journeys.outcome: The user moves tasks reversibly between Active and Completed while counts and status-specific fields stay correct.
steps: Complete an active task with its checkbox.
See it leave Active, enter Completed with muted styling and a backend-assigned completion time, and lose priority.
Sort Completed tasks by an allowed key and direction.
Reactivate the task and see it return to Active at highest priority with completion time cleared.
Observe both tab counts update after each transition.

primary_journeys.outcome: The user cannot access another account's data and can end access to protected pages.
steps: Use task operations only within the authenticated account's ownership scope.
Receive not-found behavior for a task that does not exist or is not owned by the account.
Log out and return to Login.
Remain unable to access protected content with the invalidated or expired session.

primary_journeys.outcome: The operator starts and restarts the local stack without seeded data or loss of persisted user data.
steps: Supply required local configuration and run docker compose up.
Observe frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL services start and Flyway migrations apply automatically.
Confirm the first startup has no users or tasks.
Create data, recreate ordinary service containers, and confirm the named PostgreSQL volume retains it.

goals.statement: Enable each registered user to manage only their own active and completed tasks.
Keep task validation, lifecycle transitions, timestamps, sorting, and active priority deterministic and backend-authoritative.
Run the complete stack locally with Docker Compose and preserve PostgreSQL data in a named volume.
Map Studio to the canonical GitHub repository and track appropriate delivery work through current issues and milestones.

success_criteria.statement: The complete empty-state application starts locally and applies its schema automatically.
success_criteria.measurement: From an empty database with required configuration supplied, docker compose up starts frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL; Flyway completes; user and task row counts are zero.

success_criteria.statement: Registration, login, logout, and invalid-session handling follow the settled account flow.
success_criteria.measurement: Acceptance scenarios verify registration redirects to Login without a session, normalized duplicate email is rejected, valid login opens Active, and logout or expiry prevents protected access.

success_criteria.statement: No user can read or mutate another user's tasks.
success_criteria.measurement: A two-user authorization test exercises every task read and mutation capability and receives no foreign task data, with direct foreign IDs producing not-found behavior.

success_criteria.statement: Users immediately see saved priority and can create, edit, delete, sort, and deliberately reorder valid active tasks with correct visible state.
success_criteria.measurement: Acceptance scenarios cover Priority/highest-first as the Active frontend default, a visible dedicated grip as the sole drag origin, validation bounds, immediate list/count updates, delete confirmation, every Active sort direction, and persisted contiguous priority after reload and later login.

success_criteria.statement: Completion and reactivation preserve immutable task data while updating status-specific data and views.
success_criteria.measurement: Acceptance scenarios verify completion time and priority removal on completion, read-only Completed behavior, all Completed sorts, and highest-priority assignment with cleared completion time on reactivation.

success_criteria.statement: Accounts and tasks survive ordinary Compose restarts and container recreation.
success_criteria.measurement: After creating at least one account and task, recreate the application and database containers without deleting the named volume and verify the same account and task remain available.

success_criteria.statement: The minimal interface remains usable with conventional controls on ordinary desktop and mobile viewport sizes.
success_criteria.measurement: UI review at representative desktop and mobile widths confirms readable content, visible keyboard focus, clear labels, reachable actions, and no viewport-blocking layout failures.

success_criteria.statement: The Studio project and appropriate delivery records are traceable in the canonical GitHub repository.
success_criteria.measurement: Verify repository mapping to https://github.com/prashant7163/tasks-list and that agreed stages have milestones with scoped issues carrying acceptance criteria, status, and relevant implementation or evidence links.

non_goals: Deploying or hosting the application in the cloud or designing a multi-server architecture.
Adding due dates, reminders, notifications, user-entered completion dates, or calendar behavior.
Adding tags, categories, projects, subtasks, search, extra filters, pagination, or infinite scrolling.
Adding attachments, rich text, collaboration, task sharing, multiple assignees, analytics, audit history, or seeded demo data.
Adding email verification, password recovery, profile management, account deletion, administrative screens, social login, or third-party product integrations.
Creating a native mobile client, elaborate branding, or a UI component framework.
Prescribing capacity, scalability, performance targets, an automated-test framework, or an exact dependency version during discovery.
scope_included: React/Vite frontend with Sign Up, Login, and a protected task view containing Active and Completed tabs, per-tab counts, and independent sort controls.
Spring Boot REST backend with Spring Security server-side sessions, CSRF protection, ownership enforcement, validation, task lifecycle logic, sorting, and transactional priority updates.
PostgreSQL persistence through JPA/Hibernate and automatically applied Flyway migrations.
Registration with display name, normalized case-insensitive unique email, adaptively hashed password, and redirect to Login without automatic authentication.
Active task creation, editing, confirmed permanent deletion, completion, reversible sorting, and immediately discoverable mouse drag-and-drop priority ordering through a dedicated visible grip.
Completed task display with muted styling, reversible sorting, read-only behavior except reactivation, and backend-controlled completion timestamps.
Docker Compose orchestration for frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL, with an empty initial database and a named database volume.
Clean human-readable logging with rolling log files.
Canonical GitHub repository mapping plus useful issue and milestone tracking for delivery stages, implementable work, defects, actionable decisions, and acceptance follow-ups.
scope_excluded: Email-format validation and password-strength or complexity rules beyond required, nonblank input and normal defensive size limits.
Editing or deleting completed tasks, or assigning priority to completed tasks.
Trusting frontend validation or authorization as enforcement of business rules.
Drag-and-drop outside the normal highest-to-lowest Priority view; the reverse Priority view may disable reordering.
Ceremonial or duplicate tracking artifacts that do not add delivery value.

functional_requirements.statement: The system shall register an account from a required display name, email, and password while enforcing normalized email uniqueness and safe password storage.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Blank or whitespace-only display name, email, or password is rejected with a clear field-level error.
Surrounding email whitespace is trimmed and email lookup and uniqueness are case-insensitive, so differently capitalized forms cannot create distinct accounts.
The stored credential is only an adaptive Spring Security password hash and never the plaintext password.
Successful registration creates the account, shows success, creates no authenticated session, and redirects to Login.

functional_requirements.statement: The system shall authenticate by email and password using a server-side session and provide current-user, logout, and protected-route behavior.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Invalid credentials return one generic error that does not disclose whether the email exists.
Valid credentials create a server-side session in an HTTP-only cookie and redirect to the Active tab.
Unauthenticated access to protected content and an expired or invalid session return the UI to Login; authenticated access to public auth routes may redirect to tasks.
Logout invalidates the server-side session and returns the user to Login, after which protected content is inaccessible.

functional_requirements.statement: The backend shall scope every task read and mutation to the authenticated owner without disclosing foreign task existence.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Across list, edit, delete, complete, reactivate, and reorder capabilities, one registered user cannot view or change another user's tasks.
A requested task that is absent or not owned by the authenticated user produces the same not-found behavior.

functional_requirements.statement: The protected task view shall show the signed-in identity, Logout, task creation access, and separate Active and Completed tabs with independent counts and sort controls.

acceptance_criteria.statement: After login the Active tab is selected and shows only active tasks in Priority highest-first order, the user's display name, Logout, creation access, its count, Active sort controls, and visible reorder grips when tasks exist.
The Completed tab shows only completed tasks, its own count and sort controls, and readable muted grayscale task styling.
Active cards show completion, title, description, creation date, edit, and delete; Completed cards show title, description, creation date, completion date, and Reactivate.

functional_requirements.statement: The system shall let users create, edit, and permanently delete their own active tasks under the settled field and state rules.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Creation and editing reject a blank title or description, a title over 120 characters, or a description over 1,000 characters with clear field-level errors.
A valid new task is ACTIVE with backend-assigned immutable creation time and highest active priority, and appears with an updated count without a full page reload.
Editing is limited to active tasks and changes title or description without changing creation time or priority.
Deleting is limited to active tasks; cancel leaves the task unchanged, while confirmation permanently deletes it and closes any active-priority gap.

functional_requirements.statement: The system shall support valid, reversible transitions between ACTIVE and COMPLETED while preserving owner, content, and creation time.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Completing an active task sets COMPLETED and backend current completion time, clears priority, moves it between tabs, and updates both counts.
A completed task has no priority and cannot be edited or deleted.
Reactivating a completed task sets ACTIVE, clears completion time, assigns highest active priority, moves it between tabs, and updates both counts.
Completing an already completed task or reactivating an active task is rejected without changing persisted state.

functional_requirements.statement: The system shall maintain a unique contiguous priority order for each user's active tasks and persist authorized mouse drag-and-drop reorder operations transactionally.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Within each user's active tasks, lower numeric positions mean higher priority and positions remain unique and contiguous beginning at 1.

In the normal highest-first Priority view, every active task has a clearly visible dedicated mouse grip; only that grip initiates press-and-hold dragging, while the task item remains the drop surface.
The backend validates that every reordered task is active and owned by the authenticated user, then commits the entire order transactionally or rejects it without partial changes.
A successful reordered priority survives reload and later login; reverse Priority sorting is only a reversed presentation and may disable drag-and-drop.

Each enabled grip has a bounded pointer target at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, a graphic with at least 3:1 contrast against the card, grab/grabbing cursor feedback, and no overlap with task content or controls.
The default Priority highest-first Active view preserves the established empty-state copy when no active tasks exist.

functional_requirements.statement: The system shall provide only the allowed, reversible, case-insensitive task sort choices, with presentation sorting separate from saved priority.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The frontend Active view defaults to Priority highest-first and supports both directions for creation date, priority, and case-insensitive title; the backend omitted-query default remains unchanged.
Completed defaults to completion newest-first and supports both directions for completion date, creation date, and case-insensitive title.
Changing a sort choice does not mutate task state or saved priority; only an explicit valid reorder changes priority.
An unsupported sort key or direction is rejected and is never interpolated into an unsafe dynamic query.

functional_requirements.statement: The backend shall expose REST capabilities for authentication, current identity, status-specific task lists and counts, task mutations, lifecycle transitions, and active reorder.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The API provides register, login, logout, current identity, list Active, list Completed, create, edit, delete, complete, reactivate, and reorder capabilities.
List responses or an equivalent small summary capability provide enough information to render both tab counts after reads and mutations.

functional_requirements.statement: The Studio project shall map to the canonical GitHub repository and use useful issues and milestones as current delivery records.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The mapped canonical repository is https://github.com/prashant7163/tasks-list.
One or more GitHub milestones represent the agreed first-version delivery stages.
Implementable work, defects, actionable decisions, and acceptance follow-ups use scoped issues with clear titles, descriptions, acceptance criteria, and applicable milestone assignments.

Relevant branches, commits, pull requests, test evidence, and decision notes link to satisfying issues, whose states are reconciled idempotently to reflect planned, active, blocked, and complete work without duplicate ceremony.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Authentication, session, CSRF, validation, ownership, password, and error controls shall protect credentials and private task data at the local web trust boundary.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Session cookies are HTTP-only with appropriate same-site settings, and state-changing requests enforce CSRF protection.
The backend independently enforces authentication, ownership, field bounds, allowed sorts, state transitions, timestamps, and reorder validity.
User-facing errors and logs expose neither stack traces, plaintext passwords, session identifiers, nor unnecessary sensitive values.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The application shall persist and expose only the account and task data required by the settled first-version scope.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Persisted product data is limited to required identity, password hash, task content, ownership, current status, current priority, and creation or completion timestamps.
No audit trail, state-change history, analytics, foreign task data, or credential existence signal is exposed.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The frontend shall provide a minimal responsive interface with clear labels, visible focus, readable states, and conventional form and button behavior.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Sign Up, Login, Active, and Completed views remain readable and operable at representative ordinary desktop and mobile viewport sizes.

Interactive controls have clear labels and visible keyboard focus, muted Completed styling retains readable contrast, and the mouse-only drag grip remains visually discoverable without falsely presenting keyboard-button semantics.
Form validation and backend failures are associated with understandable fields or actions and do not rely only on color.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Task state changes shall be transactional and unexpected server or database failures shall preserve previously committed data.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Create, edit, delete, complete, reactivate, and especially multi-task priority reorder either commit their intended valid state fully or leave existing persisted state unchanged.
An unexpected server or database error returns a generic retry message and does not partially apply the attempted mutation.
A named volume mounted at PostgreSQL's data directory retains users and tasks across ordinary service restart and container recreation.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The application shall be locally operable as frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL services through Docker Compose with automatic schema migration and useful rolling logs.

acceptance_criteria.statement: With required local configuration supplied, docker compose up starts every required service without requiring demo or seeded data.
Backend startup automatically applies mutually compatible Flyway migrations to an empty or existing database.
Application logging is clean and human-readable and uses rolling files so ordinary operation does not create an unbounded single log file.

non_functional_requirements.statement: The implementation shall keep clear frontend, backend, database-migration, and local-orchestration boundaries in one repository without speculative infrastructure.

acceptance_criteria.statement: React/Vite code resides under frontend, Spring Boot code under backend, and Compose configuration declares the frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL services.
Implementation selects stable mutually compatible releases for the approved stack and records the selected versions in normal build manifests.
The first version contains no cloud, multi-server, scalability, component-library, or unrelated product scaffolding.

components: React with Vite for the frontend
Plain CSS without a component library
Human-readable clean logging with rolling logs

alternatives.name: JWT authentication
alternatives.rationale: Explicitly rejected in favor of server-side sessions for this small local-first application.

alternatives.name: Frontend component library
alternatives.rationale: Explicitly excluded; plain CSS is sufficient for the minimal interface.

alternatives.name: Cloud or multi-server deployment
alternatives.rationale: Explicitly excluded because the required runtime is local Docker Compose.

chosen_stack.rationale: The application owner settled this conventional small full-stack stack; it supports backend-authoritative sessions and validation, relational persistence and migrations, a lightweight responsive UI, and reproducible local startup without speculative infrastructure.

responsive_behavior: Use a clean minimal layout that remains readable and operable on ordinary desktop and mobile viewport sizes. Active opens in Priority highest-first with visible non-overlapping mouse drag grips when tasks exist; Completed retains completion newest-first. Preserve visible counts, sort controls, forms, buttons, focus states, and no horizontal overflow; touch reorder is not implied.
design_system_direction: Plain CSS with no component library, elaborate branding, or decorative product work. Use clear labels, conventional controls, visible focus states, readable muted grayscale styling for Completed tasks, and a clearly bounded high-contrast drag grip whose graphic has at least 3:1 contrast against the card.

external_systems.name: GitHub repository https://github.com/prashant7163/tasks-list
external_systems.purpose: Canonical source repository and delivery tracking through issues, milestones, branches, commits, pull requests, evidence links, and decision notes.

data_classifications: Account identity data: display name and normalized email
Authentication secrets: plaintext password in transit only, adaptive password hash at rest, and server-side session identifier
Private user content: task title and description
Task metadata: ownership, status, active priority, creation time, and completion time
Operational data: redacted application logs and generic error details
Delivery metadata: GitHub issues, milestones, links, status, and evidence references
settled_decisions: The application is deliberately small, local-first, and delivered as a full-stack web application in one repository.
Authentication uses Spring Security server-side sessions rather than JWT; registration does not sign the user in.
The backend is authoritative for authentication, ownership, validation, state changes, timestamps, sorting inputs, and priority.
Completion is reversible, Completed tasks are read-only except reactivation, and reactivated tasks return at highest active priority.
PostgreSQL data persists through a named Docker volume and Flyway migrations run during backend startup.
The canonical GitHub repository and GitHub issue and milestone tracking requirements are fixed.
No unresolved product questions remain within the stated scope.
Active and Completed use separate tabs and independent sorting; the Active frontend default is Priority highest-first and the Completed default is completion newest-first.
A clearly visible grip is the sole mouse drag origin; the task item remains the drop surface, and keyboard or touch reorder remains outside scope.
The backend omitted-query sort default, REST contract, authorization, database schema, and transactional priority rules remain unchanged.
GitHub issues 4 through 6 close with prior accepted evidence; issue 7 remains open until this exact fix completes ordered assurance.
assumptions: Implementation can select stable mutually compatible dependency releases available when work begins without changing the approved technology stack.
Implementation can select normal defensive maximum sizes for registration fields that do not introduce product-level email-format or password-strength rules.
The local operator will supply required non-secret configuration and keep credentials or environment secrets outside repository and Studio state.
The delivery operator will have authorized access to map the Studio project and maintain issues and milestones in the canonical GitHub repository.

Ordinary mobile viewport usability applies to the responsive web interface; the specified priority reorder interaction is mouse drag-and-drop and does not imply a native mobile or touch-reorder requirement.
Exact REST route names may follow established Spring conventions as long as every required capability and behavior remains available.
constraints: Use one repository with frontend and backend directories and Docker Compose configuration for frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL.
Run locally through Docker Compose; cloud hosting and multi-server architecture are outside scope.
Start the first empty database without seeded users or tasks and mount a named volume at PostgreSQL's data directory.
Store timestamps in UTC and let the frontend format them for display.
Title is required, nonblank, and at most 120 characters; description is required, nonblank, and at most 1,000 characters.
Email comparison and uniqueness are case-insensitive after trimming and normalization, with no product-level email-format validation.
Passwords have no product-level strength rule but must never be stored in plaintext.
No prescribed performance, capacity, multi-server, automated-test framework, or test-coverage percentage target may be inferred.
Only exact explicit human approval of the final specification digest may move this draft across the approval boundary.
risks: A missing ownership predicate on any task route could expose or mutate another user's private tasks; mitigate with centralized authenticated-owner queries and two-user tests across every capability.
Session-cookie or CSRF misconfiguration could permit unauthorized state changes; mitigate through an Architect-reviewed threat model and security-focused integration tests.

Concurrent task creation, completion, deletion, reactivation, or reorder could produce duplicate or gapped priorities; mitigate with database constraints or locking as appropriate and transactional invariant tests.
Dynamic sort handling could become an injection or correctness vector; mitigate by mapping an explicit allowlist of keys and directions to typed backend sort definitions.
Container recreation could lose data if the named volume is mis-mounted or removed; mitigate with explicit Compose configuration and a persistence acceptance test.
Frontend and backend state may diverge after failed mutations; mitigate by applying UI updates only from successful authoritative responses and presenting safe retry feedback.
Logs could leak credentials, session identifiers, or task content; mitigate with redaction rules and verification of authentication and error log paths.
A nested draggable element could leave whole-card dragging enabled; mitigate by making only the grip draggable, retaining the wrapper only as a drop surface, and testing forbidden drag origins.
Defaulting to the priority component could suppress the existing empty state; mitigate with an explicit empty-state regression test.
A stronger grip could overlap content at narrow widths or remain subjectively faint; mitigate with desktop/mobile layout checks plus computed target-size and contrast evidence.

Changing the frontend default could regress confirmed-sort race protection or authoritative reconciliation; mitigate by retaining and rerunning pending-load, rejected-load, success, cancellation, reload, and later-login tests.
GitHub tracking can become stale or ceremonial; mitigate with fresh live readback and idempotent evidence-linked reconciliation at delivery gates.
dependencies: A local Docker Engine with Docker Compose support.
Stable mutually compatible React, Vite, Java, Spring Boot, Spring Security, JPA/Hibernate, PostgreSQL, Flyway, and build-tool releases selected during implementation.
Browser support for standard responsive web behavior, HTTP cookies, conventional forms, and the required mouse drag-and-drop interaction.
Authorized GitHub access to https://github.com/prashant7163/tasks-list for later repository mapping and governed issue and milestone operations.
An Architect threat-model artifact covering account data, credentials, server-side sessions, CSRF, browser-to-backend trust, and per-user task authorization before specification approval.
A UX flow artifact for responsive authentication, Active and Completed views, validation, confirmation, session expiry, and mutation-failure states before implementation planning.

materially_affected_specialists.reason: The approved behavior change must be captured in a bounded, traceable run-specific specification.
The frontend interaction and superseding UI-default clause require confirmation that public API, data, and threat boundaries remain unchanged.
The visible grip, pointer target, contrast, and responsive non-overlap behavior require interaction review.
The implementation and regression tests are confined to the React/Vite frontend.
The code-producing frontend task requires independent exact-candidate review.
The exact frontend candidate requires reproducible test and production-build evidence.
Desktop and mobile-width behavior, drag initiation, persistence, rollback, and regression scope require independent verification.
The completed task and GitHub reconciliation require identity-independent evidence tracing reported only to the Orchestrator.
